name: navigator-no-unguarded-main-git
body:
The distributed `codebase-navigator` holds a git grant set free of any form that rewrites the main checkout's branch refs or moves its HEAD/working tree and bypasses the verify gate. Integration of a change-set into main happens ONLY through `apg project merge <name>` (verify gate → merge → main rebuild → self-clean).

The template's frontmatter `bash:` block (`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`) carries the read-only patterns below. A grant the spec calls read-only admits zero ref-writing forms.

The grant set (per verb):
- `git merge` sits outside the grant set — merging into main is `apg project merge`'s job, behind the verify gate.
- `git checkout` and `git switch` sit outside the grant set — they move the main checkout's HEAD/working tree; the flow reaches its goals with the project branch in its worktree and `apg project start` creating it.
- `git worktree *` narrows to read-only listing (`git worktree list *`) — worktree add/remove belongs to `apg project start` / `apg project merge`'s self-clean.
- The blanket `git branch *` narrows to the exact, genuinely read-only pattern `git branch --show-current` (it prints the checked-out branch and takes zero ref-writing option). The blanket `git branch *` sits outside the grant set because it admits ref-writing forms — `git branch -f <branch> <sha>`, `git branch -D`, `git branch -m`. Branch listing stays outside the grant set: the branch/worktree identity comes from `apg project start`'s printed path and `git status`, so the single exact inspection pattern removes the ref-rewrite risk entirely. A grant the spec calls read-only admits zero rewriting of a branch ref.
- `git rebase *` stays granted — the agent-builder main-flow step "rebase the project worktree onto main" uses it; the template states it runs with cwd INSIDE the project worktree (rebasing the project branch onto main) and keeps the main checkout out of the flow.
- Read-only `git status *`, `git diff *`, `git log *` stay granted — with one caveat: `git diff *` and `git log *` admit the output-redirect option `--output=<file>`, which writes an arbitrary file (including inside the main checkout). `--output=<file>` is FORBIDDEN on every granted git verb; the navigator runs `git diff` and `git log` to stdout only. This is a prose-enforced known risk (the glob reaches zero exclusion of the form), recorded in `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only` alongside the worktree-only `git rebase` rule.

Acceptance criteria:
- The navigator template's frontmatter `bash:` block grants zero of `git merge`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, a blanket `git branch`, or unrestricted `git worktree`; the read-only git patterns it grants are exactly `git status *`, `git diff *`, `git log *`, `git branch --show-current`, and `git worktree list *`, plus `git rebase *` for the worktree-only sync.
- The navigator passes `--output=<file>` (or any output-redirecting option) to a granted git verb zero times; `git diff`/`git log` output goes to stdout only, and `requirements.constraint.main-integration-via-merge-gate-only` states this forbidden form and records it as a known risk exactly as it does for the worktree-only `git rebase` rule.
- Its body states that main is integrated only via `apg project merge`, and that `git rebase` runs only inside the project worktree for the agent-builder sync step.
- `AGENTS.md` states the same (its "Worktree isolation" section calls a blanket `git branch` a read-only verb zero times).
- Scope: `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` sit outside this requirement.
